Q: codeigniter - using helper in controller doesn't work A:

Helpers are the ideal way to declare global functions in codeigniter and what you are doing is correct. Following are just few points that will help you.

  • Load all helpers through single line instead of separate lines.

    $this->load->helper('form');
$this->load->helper('url');
$this->load->helper('login');
    $this->load->helper(array('form','url','login'));

  • If you want to make it global across all the controller files, then you can put it in the autoload.php file located in 'config/' directory. Update the $autoload['helper'] variable as follows:

    $autoload['helper'] = array('url','site');

Source: How to create & call global PHP functions in CodeIgniter

Q: self.setCentralWidget() places my widget in top left not center A:

setCentralWidget makes the widget fill the entire center region rather than centering it inside that space. Since you gave main a fixed size of 250×500, it stays stuck in the top-left corner.

I'd wrap main in a container and use a layout to handle the alignment. Set that container as the central widget instead:

from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt

# … after creating main and its layout …
container = QWidget()
container_layout = QVBoxLayout(container)
container_layout.addWidget(main, alignment=Qt.AlignCenter)
self.setCentralWidget(container)

So the fixed-size widget stays centered regardless of the window size.

Q: Why is CompileFlags from .clangd file not applied to my VS Code build task? A:

The CompileFlags in your .clangd only modify the arguments that the clangd language server uses internally for in-editor analysis (diagnostics, completion, etc.). They are not passed to the compiler when your VS Code task runs clang.exe - the task invokes the compiler directly and does not consult clangd. That's why the output shows no -std=c23 or warning flags.

To keep build flags and analysis in sync without duplicating them in tasks.json, let a build system own the flags and produce a compile_commands.json. clangd reads that database automatically. The build task can then call the build system instead of bare clang.

For CMake, your project would have a CMakeLists.txt:

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.15)
project(my_app C)
add_executable(my_app main.c)
target_compile_options(my_app PRIVATE -std=c23 -Wall -Wextra)

Generate the build directory once:

cmake -B build -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON

And change your task to use CMake:

{
  "label": "Build C (msys64-clang64)",
  "type": "process",
  "command": "cmake",
  "args": ["--build", "build", "--target", "my_app"]
}

Now flags are defined in one place. clangd sees them via compile_commands.json, and the actual build picks them up from the CMake configuration.

Q: spring boot ssl client cert fails with PKIX path building failed error A:

If you install the certificate on the server's keystore, the tomcat server will take care of handshaking the ssl cert with the target machine, you dont have to load it in the code every time you invoke a service.

Q: How to set the Usb connection mode? A:

For anyone having this issue with an HTC One M8, this is a bit off the wall, but makes the point to think outside the box. A USB connection resulted in the device charging, that was it.

The solution was the combination of a different USB cable, uninstalling an application called Battery Doctor (which apparently likes to manage everything around your battery), AND USB Network Setting - turn ON Smart Network Sharing...Seemingly unrelated...but this combination got my connected with MobileGo for Android to manage and back up files,contacts and settings.
